records.text: Acid rain is precipitation with higher-than-normal acidity caused by air pollutants; it can fall as rain, snow, or other precipitation.

The main causes of acid rain are sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx), released primarily by burning fossil fuels such as coal and oil. In the atmosphere, these pollutants react with water, oxygen, and other chemicals to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid.
Acid rain can alter soil and water pH, harm trees and plants, damage aquatic habitats, reduce plant growth, and diminish biodiversity.
Acid rain can irritate the lungs and make breathing difficult, particularly for people with respiratory conditions such as asthma.

Acid rain can corrode buildings, bridges, and other infrastructure, leading to repair and replacement costs; damage to crops and forests can also reduce agricultural and forestry revenue and productivity.

Acid rain can be mitigated by reducing sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide emissions through measures such as clean energy sources, including wind and solar power, and emissions controls on industrial sources.

Endangered species are animals, plants, and other organisms at risk of becoming extinct in the near future. Biodiversity loss and species extinction can negatively affect ecosystems, food security, and human well-being.

Life sciences study living organisms and include fields such as biology, ecology, genetics, and conservation biology. Research in these fields studies why species decline and develops strategies to conserve endangered species and biodiversity.

Approaches to endangered-species conservation include protecting and restoring habitats such as forests, wetlands, and coral reefs; captive breeding and reintroduction; genetic management to preserve diversity and prevent inbreeding; public education and outreach; and policies and governance to protect species and habitats.
